candidates.attacker_control: Fully remote and unauthenticated. The attacker controls the `url` query parameter of a web-component bootstrap request, e.g. `GET /<ctx>/web-component/web-component-ui.html?url=https://evil.example/%3C/script%3E%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C/script%3E/x/web-component/web-component-ui.html`. The application decodes the parameter and uses the substring up to the first `/web-component/web-component` occurrence, yielding `//evil.example/</script><script>alert(1)</script>/` as the service URL. No session or authentication is required beyond the framework creating a session for the bootstrap request.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Considered that `checkURL` (WebComponentBootstrapHandler:395-404) rejects only double quotes and is invoked only from `modifyPath` for `src` attribute rewriting in the JS transfer, so it does not protect this path; considered that JSON stringification escapes quotes/backslashes, which it does, but the explicit manual `<` -> `\x3C` escaping applied only to `initialUIDL` at BootstrapHandler:1342 shows the serializer itself does not escape `<`; considered that in npm mode the response is JavaScript and `innerHTML`-inserted `<script>` does not execute, so the strongest variant is the compatibility-mode HTML bootstrap; considered that the tainted value must contain a literal `/web-component/web-component` for the substring to succeed, which the attacker fully controls.
candidates.impact: Cross-site scripting in the Vaadin application origin: an attacker who lures a victim to the crafted URL can execute arbitrary JavaScript in that victim's browser session (session/CSRF token theft, actions on behalf of the victim, content spoofing). In compatibility mode the crafted link alone returns an HTML page containing the executed script; in npm mode the tainted value reaches an `innerHTML` sink in the embedding page.
candidates.prerequisites: Application exports at least one web component (so WebComponentBootstrapHandler is registered) and the crafted request path matches `.*/web-component-(ui|bootstrap)\.(js|html)$`. The high-impact reflected variant requires compatibility (bower) mode so that `synchronizedHandleRequest` delegates to the parent that serves a full text/html bootstrap page; the npm variant delivers the same tainted value inside the `headElem.innerHTML="…"` JavaScript transfer where `inlineHTML` does not neutralise `<`/`</script>`.
candidates.root_cause: `WebComponentBootstrapHandler.getServiceUrl(VaadinRequest, VaadinResponse)` takes the raw request parameter `url` (REQ_PARAM_URL, line 68), truncates it at the first occurrence of `/web-component/web-component`, strips the scheme and returns it as the application `serviceUrl` without validating characters or origin. `createAndInitUI` stores that value into the bootstrap application parameters (`config.put(ApplicationConstants.SERVICE_URL, serviceUrl)`, line 178). `BootstrapHandler.getBootstrapJS` serializes the application parameters with `JsonUtil.stringify` and injects the result into the inline bootstrap script (`var config = {{CONFIG_JSON}};`), and it only escapes `<` for the initial UIDL string (line 1342), not for the config JSON. The script element content is emitted raw through a jsoup DataNode, so a `</script>` sequence in the tainted config value terminates the inline script and allows an injected script element to execute in the application origin (compatibility mode), or breaks out of the `headElem.innerHTML="..."` transfer string produced by `writeBootstrapPage`/`inlineHTML` (npm mode, where only backslashes and double quotes are escaped).
candidates.title: Reflected/DOM XSS via unvalidated `url` parameter in WebComponentBootstrapHandler service URL embedded unescaped in bootstrap config JSON
candidates.trace: 1) Request parameter `url` read unfiltered at WebComponentBootstrapHandler:435 and turned into `serviceUrl` at :440-446. 2) `createAndInitUI` (:154-178) puts it into the application parameters that become the client-side `config` object and also into the push URL. 3) In compatibility mode `synchronizedHandleRequest` (:201-203) delegates to `BootstrapHandler.synchronizedHandleRequest`, which renders the page via `pageBuilder.getBootstrapPage(context)` and writes `document.outerHtml()` as text/html (:468-481). 4) `BootstrapHandler.getBootstrapJS` (:1318-1362) replaces `{{CONFIG_JSON}}` with the JSON string of the tainted appConfig; only the `initialUIDL` JSON is `<`-escaped (:1342). 5) The script is created with a raw jsoup `DataNode` (:1185-1192), so `<` is not escaped in the emitted HTML; the browser terminates the inline script at the injected `</script>` and executes the following `<script>` element in the application's origin. In npm mode the same tainted JSON is copied by `writeBootstrapPage` (:294-298) through `inlineHTML` (:406-421), which escapes only `\` and `"`, into `headElem.innerHTML`, allowing DOM-based execution in the embedding page.
candidates.unverified: Exploitability was not executed or runtime-confirmed. The exact decoding behaviour of the servlet container for percent-encoded `<`/`>` in query parameters, and jsoup's raw output of DataNode script content (external dependency not in the snapshot), were reasoned from source and from the explicit escaping comment at BootstrapHandler:1333-1342 rather than observed. Whether a later upstream fix specifically addressed this path could not be checked offline. It is also unverified whether the benchmark's target issue is this path or a different flow-server issue.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting); root cause also CWE-20/CWE-116

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot (1891 visible files; 1396 Java files parsed by the P1 index; tests under */src/test are absent from the snapshot). I inspected flow-server request handling in depth: VaadinService request pipeline and session/CSRF logic, BootstrapHandler and BootstrapHandlerHelper, WebComponentBootstrapHandler/WebComponentProvider/WebComponentGenerator/WebComponentBinding, UidlRequestHandler, ServerRpcHandler and the RPC handlers, StreamRequestHandler/StreamResourceHandler/StreamReceiverHandler, PushHandler/PushRequestHandler, StaticFileServer/ResponseWriter/HandlerHelper, DevModeHandler/DevServerWatchDog, PwaHandler/PwaRegistry, UnsupportedBrowserHandler, installer classes (NodeInstaller/DefaultArchiveExtractor/DefaultFileDownloader), plus selected flow-data/flow-maven-plugin/flow-client areas surfaced by the relations index. The P1 index is partial and syntax-only (no control/data-flow, no semantic resolution, Spring/DI and runtime reachability unverified), and its security_call facts are name-based navigation hints, not findings; areas not covered include most flow-client GWT/TS runtime behaviour, flow-migration, flow-osgi and all excluded test sources.
limitations: No code was executed, built, or deployed; the candidate is a source-level lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.
External library internals (elemental.json JsonUtil, jsoup DataNode output, servlet-container query-parameter decoding) are not in the snapshot and were reasoned about from usage and comments.
The P1 relation index reports partial coverage and does not implement data/control flow or semantic resolution; absence of an index record was never treated as proof that an area is safe.
Repository tests are excluded from the snapshot, so no regression test or security test could be used to confirm expected behaviour.
The compatibility-mode (bower) precondition for the strongest reflected variant could not be validated against a running application.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip-slip in DefaultArchiveExtractor.extractZipArchive (flow-server .../installer/DefaultArchiveExtractor.java:81-98): the tar branch verifies `startsWithPath(destPath.getCanonicalPath(), canonicalDestinationDirectory)` (lines 134-148) but the zip branch concatenates `entry.getName()` and writes without a canonical-path check.
rejected_leads.reason: Real code-level CWE-22 asymmetry, but the archive is normally fetched over HTTPS from the hard-coded nodejs.org download root (NodeInstaller.DEFAULT_NODEJS_DOWNLOAD_ROOT) and only affects build/startup file writing; attacker control requires a malicious/misconfigured download root or MITM, which is materially weaker than the request-time XSS. Left as an unconfirmed lead, not a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirect / header injection in VaadinServlet.handleContextOrServletRootWithoutSlash (flow-server .../server/VaadinServlet.java:314-343) building the Location header from `request.getRequestURI()` and the raw query string (only CR/LF stripped).
rejected_leads.reason: Exploitation depends on the servlet container accepting absolute-form request targets so getRequestURI() returns an off-host URI; request/response splitting is explicitly mitigated by stripping CR/LF. Not clearly reachable with a trustworthy source-level guarantee, so rejected.

rejected_leads.lead: NumberFormatException in ResponseWriter.isQualityValueZero (flow-server .../internal/ResponseWriter.java:525-541) when Accept-Encoding contains e.g. `gzip;q=abc`, causing an unhandled runtime exception during static resource serving.
rejected_leads.reason: At most a per-request error/DoS of low impact; no state corruption or data exposure demonstrated. Rejected as too weak.

rejected_leads.lead: DevModeHandler.serveDevModeRequest copies all client request headers and the webpack response headers (flow-server .../server/DevModeHandler.java:342-385) and builds the upstream URL as `http://localhost:<port>` + path after `isPathUnsafe`/quote checks.
rejected_leads.reason: Dev-mode only; restricted/ignored headers on HttpURLConnection and the path checks make a concrete attacker-controlled SSRF/header-injection effect unproven. Rejected.

rejected_leads.lead: JavaScript string injection via unescaped default property values in WebComponentGenerator.getDefaultJsValue (flow-server .../server/webcomponent/WebComponentGenerator.java:252-279) escaping only single quotes, not backslashes.
rejected_leads.reason: The value originates from developer-written WebComponentExporter property definitions, not from an untrusted client or request, so attacker control is missing. Rejected.

summary: Reviewed the Vaadin Flow (flow-project 2.6-SNAPSHOT) snapshot, concentrating on flow-server request handling: bootstrap/web-component bootstrap, UIDL/RPC handling, CSRF/push-id checks, stream resources/receivers, static file serving, path-safety helpers, dev-mode proxy and frontend installer. The single strongest source-supported lead is a reflected/DOM cross-site scripting path in the web-component bootstrap handler: the request-controlled `url` parameter is used verbatim as the application's service URL and is then serialized into the inline bootstrap `config` JSON without HTML escaping, while the sibling `initialUIDL` JSON is explicitly `<`-escaped at the same call site. Several other suspicious spots (zip-slip in the Node archive extractor, request-URI based redirect in VaadinServlet, Accept-Encoding q-value parsing, header copy in the dev-mode proxy) were checked and rejected or kept as unconfirmed leads because attacker control or impact is materially weaker or requires unusual preconditions.
